Term1: Urethritis associated with sexually transmitted diseases
Text:
# URETHRITIS ASSOCIATED WITH SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED DISEASES

The main differential in a person who presents with dysuria is between cystitis and urethritis. Bacterial urethritis is more likely in people with mild dysuria, onset over a few days, or recent sexual contact.

The two most common sexually transmitted urethritis pathogens are Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis. Nucleic acid amplification tests for these pathogens are more sensitive than culture and should be used for patients at risk for sexually transmitted urethritis.
Chlamydia & GC PCR/LCR test

## For patients who have recently been treated for urethritis

[Treatment of recurrent or persistent urethritis](recurrent-persist-urethritis)

When dysuria is from a sexually transmitted disease, the patient's sexual partner(s) during the previous 60 days should be evaluated for sexually transmitted infection.

If diagnostic tests for the cause of urethritis are not feasible, therapy for
both N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis should be given to partners.

## Initial treatment of patients and sex partners

Patients and partners are often infected with both N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis. Treat for both pathogens unless one is ruled out by lab test.
